scope: Original Blender oath shrine, five oath crests, three wave-progress lenses, articulated reward coffer and saved-state presentation. Earned-cache placement after reload and retention after death are fixed. Broader world events and replayability remain unfinished.

geometry.space: Native model-local XYZ, positions x100; native normals retained; studio transforms omitted; crystal and lid use separate runtime pivots

native_checks.note: Final asset and expedition logic tested. Isolated-adventure preview buttons were added afterward and tested in the production UI.

visual_checks: Blender studio inspection of cut masonry, bronze inlays/astrolabe, five emblems, articulated walnut coffer and contents. Moved the three wave lenses to the right pylon for visibility beside the open lid.
Native Metal QA showed Iron shrine during real enemy animation and the three-wave test.

Release43 Settings and testing / Testing shortcuts / Oath shrine preview selected Cinder oath and Preview earned coffer; new flame crest, gold crystal, three gold wave markers and open treasure coffer rendered in Hyrule Field.
Claim equipment through the real expedition journal switched to Cache claimed; returning to the world showed the coffer still open with contents removed and the crystal restored to the Cinder color.
Storm covenant / Preview empty coffer produced the distinct lightning crest and violet crystal with empty open interior.
Release43 left paused in Equipment, backpack count rose from 35 to 36 after the single equipment claim.
binary_asset_check: All 18,529 final generated vertices and normals matched byte-for-byte in both frozen binaries. Release excludes the native expedition QA registration.
limitations: Native lit vertex colors; studio PBR metallic/roughness is preview only.
Shrine has no blocking collision and uses existing safe-ground placement.
Cache contents symbolize the reward choices; they do not create a separate rupee pickup or change reward quantities.
Reward claims still use the expedition journal. Expeditions remain solo wilderness encounters.
Native QA observes real enemies and scripted defeat callbacks; it does not prove player combat balance.
Broader scene/age coverage and crowded-scene performance remain unmeasured.
